Author: Deepak Roshan

In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Roshan
---------

For the Petitioner : Mr. Kalyan Roy, Advocate For the State : Mr. P.D. Agrawal, Spl.P.P.
---------
05/03.08.2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. This criminal revision application is directed against the judgment dated 30.08.2003 passed by the VIth Additional Sessions Judge, Hazaribagh in Criminal Appeal No. 183/89/86/2001,
dismissing the appeal and upholding the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 19.8.89 passed by the S.D.J.M., Hazaribagh in G.Case No.133/87, corresponding to T.R. No. 371/89,
whereby the petitioner has been convicted under Section 16 (1) (A) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year with a fine of Rs.1,000/- and on failure of the same, further simple imprisonment for three months.
3.

The prosecution case in brief is that on 16.05.1987, a sample of Arhar Dal and Chana Sattu was taken from the shop of the other accused person (since deceased), at whose behest the petitioner herein sold the said sample and later on the Public Analyst declared the said sample of Arhar Dal to be adulterated, inasmuch as, it contained colour.
4. At the outset, Mr. Kalyan Roy, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is not Ashok Kumar Agrawal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95907053/
1 a habitual offender and the allegation is minor in nature.

sentences.text: The Petitioner remained in custody also for about 17 days.

As such, he has confined his prayer only to the question of sentence as the occurrence is of the year 1987 and the petitioner is now an aged person and sending him back to jail at this stage even for a short period will hamper the entire family; as such the sentence may be modified for the period already undergone.
5. Learned counsel for the State supported the judgments and submits that there is no error in the finding given by the Trial Court.
As such, the conviction cannot be set aside, however, the sentence may be modified in lieu of fine.

6. After going through the impugned judgment including the lower court records and keeping in mind the limited submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the scope of revision jurisdiction, I am not inclined to interfere with the findings of the court below and as such the judgment of conviction passed by the learned trial court and upheld by the learned appellate court is, hereby, sustained.
7.

However, so far as sentence is concerned, it is apparent from record that the incident is of the year 1987 and 35 years have elapsed and the petitioner must have suffered the rigors of litigation for all these years.
It is not stated that the petitioner has ever misused the privilege of bail.
Further, the incident does not reflect any cruelty on the part of the petitioner or any mental depravity and he also remained in custody for about 17 days.

8. In a situation of this nature, I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the petitioner/convict back to prison; rather interest of justice would be sufficed if the sentence is modified to the period already undergone.
9. Thus, the sentence passed by the court below is hereby, modified to the extent that the petitioner- Ashok Kumar Agrawal is sentenced to undergo for the period already undergone.
10. The petitioner shall be discharged from the liability of his bail bond.
11. With the aforesaid observations and modification in sentence only, the instant revision application is disposed of.

12. Let the copy of this order be communicated to the court below and also to the petitioner through the officer-in- charge of concerned police station.
13. Let the lower court record be sent to the court concerned forthwith.

(Deepak Roshan, J.) sm/
